basis: Encephalopathy, ataxia and motor neuron degeneration define disease; muscle wasting is denervation-related. Optic atrophy and scoliosis occur in only 5-29%.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm and infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Blepharophimosis establishes eyelid involvement; the supplied information does not establish other affected organs.
Anorectal malformation and deafness define the syndrome; hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Renal excluded because definition explicitly states absence despite conflicting HPO.
Dysferlin-related skeletal muscle dystrophy. Cardiac findings are occasional (5-29%); respiratory involvement is excluded by the definition.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the cecal epithelium.
Reproductive system umbrella has no axis; endocrine involvement applies to selected subtypes rather than most patients across the group.
Acute infarction directly damages the posterior myocardium.
Pilocytic astrocytoma is a primary central nervous system tumor.
Androgen receptor resistance causes impaired hormonal action and abnormal sex development; reproductive anomalies do not add another axis.
Renal proximal tubulopathy; developmental delay in 3/4 and phosphate-wasting hypophosphatemia in 3/5. Enzyme elevations alone do not establish hepatic or muscle damage.
Melanoma originates in the skin; distant metastases are not defining involvement.
Autoimmune thyroid hyperfunction. Clinically significant orbitopathy is around 25-30% and separately diagnosed; transient ocular signs do not establish damage.
Congenital secretory diarrhea; hepatic steatosis with elevated transaminases in 5/5 supports liver injury, and recurrent hypoglycemia in 5/5 supports metabolic dysfunction.
Lysosomal lipid storage disorder; severe hepatic disease affects most in this perinatal form, and pulmonary infiltration with respiratory failure is common.
Theileria infects leukocytes and/or erythrocytes. The supplied definition describes livestock infection.
Fungal infection directly inflames the esophagus; underlying diabetes or immunodeficiency is a separate condition.
Inherited immunodeficiency; the record does not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Familial nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis is a renal glomerular disorder; immune causation is not established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, present in 28/28 reported patients.
Pure hair and nail ectodermal dysplasia; absent eyelashes reflect hair loss rather than intrinsic eye disease.
Inherited skeletal dysplasia affecting cranial and clavicular development; no additional organ damage is established.
Inherited myopathy, joint contractures and external ophthalmoplegia define the syndrome. Respiratory distress and dysphagia lack evidence of common direct organ damage.
Endocrine dysfunction, intellectual disability and alopecia define syndrome; sensorineural deafness is a common defining feature in the four reported siblings.
Neurodevelopmental and progressive spastic disorder with brain abnormalities. Hypotonia and spasticity are neurologic; structural joint and ocular abnormalities are rare.
